headline: High risk: Cline’s broad workspace/network/tool access can cascade into unsafe actions when paired with Taipy’s data-engineering workflows, while prompt-injection and leakage risks remain moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can read workspace files, run browsers, and use MCP, so attacker-controlled content in shared files or tool outputs could be treated as instructions. Taipy is a data-engineering app that may consume those files or outputs, creating a plausible bridge. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF Cline and Taipy share a workspace directory or file handoff path, prompt injection becomes reachable.
IF Taipy ingests Cline-produced files without sanitization, attacker text can influence downstream behavior.
mitigations: Disable shared workspace handoff between the two agents.
Require manual review of any file passed from Cline to Taipy.
Strip instructions from imported text before Taipy processes it.
Use separate directories for generated artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can write/read workspace files; Taipy has no documented data classes or egress, so leakage is mainly through shared files or copied outputs. Because the pairwise workspace bridge is plausible but not directly evidenced, medium is appropriate rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace files, Cline can expose code or screenshots to Taipy.
IF Taipy is extended to read those files into reports, sensitive content can be reproduced in outputs.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace.
Use separate OS users or containers for each agent.
Review any Taipy output before sharing externally.
Turn off browser screenshot capture when not needed.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git, and broad network egress in a per-workspace session with shared state via filesystem. Taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool, so if it also mutates the same workspace or artifacts, concurrent writes can corrupt state. The profiles do not prove locking, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF Taipy writes to the same repository or data directory as Cline, file races can occur.
IF both agents modify git state without external locking, commits or working tree state can be corrupted.
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent.
Pause one agent before the other writes shared artifacts.
Use git locks or a single-writer policy.
Review diffs before any commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutual exclusion.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits; Taipy is an automation/data-engineering system that may act on those outputs. If Taipy treats Cline’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect pipelines or actions. No verification mechanism is documented, so the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Taipy consumes Cline-generated files or summaries without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF Taipy triggers scheduled jobs from those inputs, downstream actions can be wrong at scale.
mitigations: Require human approval before Taipy acts on Cline output.
Add schema validation to all handoff files.
Compare Cline outputs against source data before use.
Log and review any automated action triggered by imported artifacts.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots and may send model-provider API keys to configured providers, while Taipy’s profile shows no touched data classes or residency constraints. The pair does not document a concrete residency or certification mismatch, so only a low compliance risk is supported from the available evidence.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Cline’s browser or workspace, compliance obligations may apply.
IF Taipy is later configured to process regulated data, retention and residency must be rechecked.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workflow.
Confirm provider and workspace retention settings for Cline.
Document data classes allowed in Taipy.
Review any API-key handling in Cline.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
